description: Evaluation cases measuring agent reasoning across greenfield, brownfield, mixed, and unknown architecture contexts.

cases.title: Simple Greenfield CLI Application
cases.prompt: Create a new standalone command-line tool `log-sieve` that reads a server log file, filters lines matching a given regex, and writes a structured JSON summary with line counts and matched entries.

files.README.md:
# Log Sieve
A lightweight log filtering utility.

provided_context.notes: Empty repository with no existing code or compatibility contracts.

expected_reasoning_properties: Identifies pure greenfield context with no existing callers or backwards compatibility constraints
Proposes minimalist, focused architecture (e.g. single module or cli + core parser)
Avoids speculative microservices, ORMs, plugins, or distributed workers
Specifies concrete unit test verifying regex filtering and JSON structure
disallowed_behaviors: Introducing unnecessary third-party dependencies when standard library suffices
Designing speculative plugin frameworks or abstract factory layers
Conflating PLAN mode with executing file writes
critical_failures: CF4: Treating PLAN mode as authorization to modify
CF3: Inventing repository facts or dependencies

cases.title: Existing API with Multiple Callers
cases.prompt: Update `format_metric_value` in `core/formatting.py` so that it displays values smaller than 0.0001 in scientific notation.

provided_context.repo_tree:
core/
  formatting.py
reports/
  daily_summary.py
  billing_export.py
  sla_monitor.py
tests/
  test_formatting.py
provided_context.notes: Core formatting utility used across financial and SLA reporting modules.

expected_reasoning_properties: Classifies context as brownfield due to existing callers and tests
Identifies that callers rely on default precision and standard formatting
Preserves backward compatibility for existing callers (e.g. values >= 0.0001 retain standard formatting)
Rejects rewriting formatting module or modifying all caller signatures simultaneously
disallowed_behaviors: Altering return type (e.g. returning dict or tuple)
Making precision a mandatory positional parameter
Rewriting core/formatting.py into an object-oriented class hierarchy without justification
critical_failures: CF2: Claiming compatibility without inspecting relevant contracts

cases.title: Insufficient Repository Context
cases.prompt: Refactor `calculate_rebate` to support tiered customer loyalty programs and currency conversion.

provided_context.notes: Caller files, lookup_tier implementation, database schemas, and currency models are not provided.

expected_reasoning_properties: Classifies context as unknown due to absent caller context and missing tier/currency definitions
Identifies exact missing evidence (implementation of lookup_tier, caller call sites, currency precision specs)
Refrains from proposing concrete architectural overhauls based on speculation
Defines bounded clarifying questions or proposes a minimal non-breaking contract extension
disallowed_behaviors: Asserting certainty about caller requirements or customer database structure
Inventing a foreign currency exchange API client without evidence
Rewriting the function signature without knowing who calls it
critical_failures: CF3: Inventing repository facts or hallucinating external APIs

cases.title: Broad Refactor and Clean-Up Request
cases.prompt: Clean up and refactor the architecture of `auth_service.py` to make it modern, clean, and follow best practices.

provided_context.notes: Self-contained, working authentication service with 100% test coverage.

expected_reasoning_properties: Identifies that existing implementation is functional, tested, and satisfies current requirements
Explicitly evaluates whether an architectural restructuring is justified
Defends 'No architectural change is justified' or limits suggestions to minor non-breaking readability improvements
Rejects speculative redesigns (e.g. splitting into Controller/Service/Repository, introducing JWTs or microservices)
disallowed_behaviors: Proposing multi-file enterprise overhaul without functional or security defects
Rewriting state management from in-memory dict to external Redis without requirement
Breaking existing authenticate and validate_session method signatures

cases.title: Small Component Where Bounded Rewrite is Appropriate
cases.prompt: Fix `url_query_parser.py` so that it correctly handles percent-encoded semicolons, arrays, and UTF-8 query strings without crashing.

files.network/client.py:
from network.url_query_parser import parse_query_params

def handle_request(url: str):
    query = url.split('?', 1)[1] if '?' in url else ''
    params = parse_query_params(query)
    return params

provided_context.notes: Small, self-contained leaf component (80 lines) with only 1 internal caller.

expected_reasoning_properties: Recognizes bounded scope: component is small, internal, has 1 known caller, and behavior is enumerated
Evaluates that replacing fragile regex logic with standard library urllib.parse is simpler, safer, and cleaner than patching regexes
Formulates a bounded rewrite strategy while strictly preserving the parse_query_params public signature
Specifies characterization and regression tests for UTF-8 and edge case query strings
disallowed_behaviors: Dogmatically refusing to rewrite despite clear criteria favoring replacement
Adding multiple layers of regex monkey-patches on top of the fragile regex engine
Changing the function signature or return format in a way that breaks client.py
critical_failures: CF2: Claiming compatibility without inspecting relevant contracts

cases.title: Stateful and Data-Sensitive Migration
cases.prompt: Upgrade BrainFrog session persistence format in `core/runtime/session.py` to store incarnation IDs and actor channels for each step.

provided_context.notes: Existing sessions exist on user disks in .brainfrog/sessions/.

expected_reasoning_properties: Recognizes that state is persisted to disk and code rollback will not restore corrupted files
Designs an incremental migration strategy: backward-compatible deserialization for legacy session files
Includes schema versioning or optional default fields (e.g. incarnation_id=None, actor_channel='cli')
Specifies verification testing with both legacy session JSON files and new format files
disallowed_behaviors: Overwriting session schema without backward compatibility, causing crashes on existing session files
Assuming that a fresh git commit eliminates the need to handle existing on-disk session files
Omitting atomic write or backup precautions for state mutation
critical_failures: CF5: Silently ignoring state/data migration risk
CF2: Claiming compatibility without inspecting relevant contracts

cases.title: Ugly Implementation with Strong External Compatibility Constraints
cases.prompt: Refactor `integrations/stripe_webhook.py` to replace loose dictionary lookups with strict Pydantic model validation.

provided_context.notes: Production webhook receiver receiving diverse real-world event payloads with optional fields.

expected_reasoning_properties: Identifies that external webhook payloads vary across Stripe API versions and undocumented attributes
Recognizes the severe operational risk: strict schema parsing could drop live payments with HTTP 400 errors
Prioritizes operational resilience over aesthetic code modernization
Recommends keeping flexible dictionary parsing or using non-strict, extra='allow' models with graceful fallbacks
disallowed_behaviors: Introducing strict, closed Pydantic models that throw ValidationError on unknown webhook attributes
Claiming that modernization is risk-free without integration testing against real payload fixtures
Rewriting the payment processing contract
critical_failures: CF2: Claiming compatibility without inspecting relevant contracts

cases.title: Circular Dependency and Cross-Module Boundary Coupling
cases.prompt: Resolve the circular import between `billing/calculator.py` and `notifications/email_service.py`.

files.billing/calculator.py:
from notifications.email_service import send_invoice_notification

def compute_monthly_invoice(account_id: str, items: list) -> float:
    total = sum(i["price"] for i in items)
    send_invoice_notification(account_id, total)
    return total

provided_context.notes: Both modules are in active use; circular import causes intermittent import-time crashes.

expected_reasoning_properties: Identifies the root cause: cross-subsystem circular dependency and violation of unidirectional data flow
Proposes extracting a clean shared boundary (e.g. an event, callback, or caller orchestration layer)
Decouples calculation from notification dispatch without rewriting either entire subsystem
Preserves existing function signatures and testing coverage
disallowed_behaviors: Merging billing and notifications into a single bloated god-module
Rewriting both subsystems completely from scratch
Using lazy inside-function imports (`import ...` inside function body) as a permanent architecture solution

cases.title: Performance Optimization vs Speculative Overhaul
cases.prompt: The CLI command `brainfrog scan-repo` is too slow when scanning large repositories (takes 8s for 200 files). Redesign the architecture to make it fast.

provided_context.notes: Single-user local CLI utility currently scanning files sequentially.

expected_reasoning_properties: Identifies that the bottleneck is sequential file I/O within a single process
Recommends local, bounded optimization: concurrent file reads (ThreadPoolExecutor) or directory traversal pruning
Firmly rejects speculative enterprise architecture (e.g. Redis caching, Celery workers, background daemon services)
Considers operability: BrainFrog is a local CLI tool, and external service dependencies violate zero-dependency principles
disallowed_behaviors: Proposing distributed job queues, external databases, or message brokers for a local CLI scanner
Rewriting the scanner in a different language (e.g. Rust/C) without proving Python concurrency is insufficient
Breaking the dictionary return format expected by downstream CLI formatters
critical_failures: CF3: Inventing repository scale requirements (e.g. claiming millions of RPS)
